description: We are a multidisciplinary team of biologists, bioinformaticians, and computer scientists united by a shared passion for scientific research, discovery, and space exploration. By bridging human physiology and behavioral science with data-driven software engineering, we aim to turn complex spaceflight health telemetry into intuitive, life-saving tools for deep-space astronauts.
summary:
To safeguard astronauts against NASA’s five spaceflight hazards—radiation, isolation, distance, altered gravity, and hostile closed environments—we developed C.O.R.E, a 100% offline-first, autonomous physiological and neurocognitive co-pilot.
Approach & Development: Using an Agile, participatory Living Lab methodology, our interdisciplinary team translated peer-reviewed NASA/ESA space medicine research into a unified Python/Streamlit telemetry console. We engineered an interoperable JSON bridge fusing objective biometrics (HRV, nocturnal SpO2, glucose, salivary sIgA) with rapid neurobehavioral assessments: the 3-minute NASA PVT-Brief, a 30-second VAS, a 15-item biological strain matrix, and passive vocal biomarkers (F0 pitch flattening and speech-to-pause ratios).
Core Insights & Innovation: Recognizing that deep-space communication delays eliminate real-time Flight Surgeon support and that astronauts frequently under-report symptoms to avoid disqualification, we prioritized non-invasive, unobtrusive detection. Crucially, we incorporated biological sex-specific algorithmic weighting (per NASA’s Sex & Gender Decadal Review), a temporal persistence multiplier to track allostatic load across 9-month mission phases, and a Crosstalk Diagnostic Engine capable of detecting environmental hazards—such as cabin CO2 pockets from combined nocturnal SpO2 drops and PVT slowing—triggering immediate non-pharmacological countermeasures and safety grounding protocols.
details:
C.O.R.E: Autonomous Space Health & Behavioral Telemetry

What It Does & How It Works

C.O.R.E is a 100% offline-first, autonomous physiological and neurocognitive digital co-pilot built for astronauts on deep-space missions (ISS/Lunar Gateway, Orion, Artemis Lunar Bases, and 520-day Mars Transits). Operating on Mission Elapsed Time (MET) check-in windows, the platform bridges two core telemetry streams via a unified local schema (crew_telemetry_sync.json):

  • Physiological & Environmental Telemetry (APP 1): Tracks nocturnal Heart Rate Variability (HRV rMSSD), nocturnal SpO2, blood pressure, fasting glucose, and salivary secretory IgA (sIgA), mapped onto an interactive, color-coded human body system radar.
  • Neurobehavioral & Cognitive Telemetry (APP 2): Combines a millisecond-accurate 3-minute NASA Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT-Brief), a 30-second Visual Analog Scale (VAS), a 15-item biological strain questionnaire (E1–E15), and passive vocal biomarker extraction (Fo pitch flattening, jitter, and speech-to-pause ratios).
  • The Crosstalk Diagnostic Engine: Correlates physiological and behavioral inputs in real time to generate tiered alerts (Tier 1 Advisory, Tier 2 Caution, Tier 3 Critical / Grounding Protocol) alongside phase-specific, non-pharmacological countermeasures.

Key Benefits

  • True Deep-Space Autonomy: Zero cloud or internet dependencies ensure uninterrupted medical and cognitive self-assessment during Moon/Mars communication blackouts.
  • Low-Friction Crew Workflow: Replaces lengthy 50-item psychological surveys with rapid 3.5-minute morning and 2-minute evening check-ins tailored to astronaut timeline pressure.
  • Actionable Safety Guardrails: Automatically enforces grounding protocols (restricting EVA, docking, or robotic arm operations) when acute cognitive exhaustion or environmental hazards are detected.

Intended Impact

  • Spaceflight Mission Safety: Prevents critical human errors by detecting hidden fatigue, cumulative allostatic load, and latent herpesvirus reactivation risks (EBV, CMV, VZV) before clinical burnout occurs.
  • Reduced Reliance on Pharmacological Sleep Aids: Promotes targeted non-pharmacological interventions—such as 460-480 nm circadian LED phototherapy, 20-minute power naps, and VR Earth/Nature relaxation—reducing the need for hypnotics (e.g., zolpidem) that carry neuropsychiatric side effects in microgravity.
  • Earth Spin-Offs (ICE Environments): Directly transferable to Antarctic research stations (e.g., Concordia), submariners, aviation crews, surgeons, emergency responders, and remote telemedicine lacking continuous connectivity.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages & Frameworks: Python 3, Streamlit (interactive space-dark telemetry UI), HTML5/CSS3, and JSON (crew_telemetry_sync.json interoperability layer).
  • Data Visualization & Precision Timing: Plotly (Scatterpolar biological system radar), Pandas, and high-resolution monotonic counters (time.perf_counter()) for millisecond PVT reaction-time accuracy.
  • Acoustic & Signal Processing: praat-parselmouth and librosa for local extraction of vocal fundamental frequency Fo), jitter, and pause ratios.
  • Hardware Integration Ready: Designed to ingest data from space-qualified and analog wearables/sensors, including Actiwatch sleep/light monitors, pulse oximeters, NDIR  cabin sensors (e.g., Sensirion SCD30/SCD41), and MEMS microphones.

How Our Project Is Creative

  • Cross-System "Crosstalk" Intelligence: Rather than treating body vitals and mental health in silos, our engine fuses both streams to diagnose environmental anomalies—such as detecting a cabin CO2 pocket when nocturnal Sp02<93% coincides with PVT slowing (>280ms) and headache.
  • Bypassing Psychological Under-Reporting: Astronauts often under-report stress to avoid mission disqualification. Passive 15–30 second voice logs detect subtle neurocognitive flattening before conscious awareness.
  • Biophilic Gamification & Temporal Persistence: Integrates a Temporal Persistence Multiplier (1–2, 3–6, and 7+ days) across a 9-month mission phase model (including the Third-Quarter Effect) alongside Resilience Streaks & XP and Cupola/VR Earth viewing ("hardwired pleasure").

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • NASA’s 5 Spaceflight Hazards & HRP Standards: Every metric, threshold, and countermeasure is anchored in peer-reviewed space medicine research (Basner & Dinges, Crucian et al., Mehta et al., Barger et al., Palinkas & Suedfeld, and NASA-STD-3001).
  • Biological Sex & Gender Calibration: Incorporating findings from the NASA Sex & Gender Decadal Review and Ronca et al. (2014), our Cognitive Readiness Score (CRS) dynamically adjusts algorithmic weights for male profiles (higher weight on objective PVT due to under-reporting tendencies) versus female profiles (heightened sensitivity to sleep latency and hormonal/oxytocin dynamics).
  • Human-Centered Participatory Design: Developed using an Agile Sprint roadmap and a Quadruple Helix / Living Lab methodology to ensure that complex neuroendocrine and immunological telemetry is translated into clear, accessible guidance that any astronaut can act upon without specialized medical training.
